text: R19.1 built and pushed (9b57156), in install/backup-windows. It's encrypted with your passphrase, lands in your Drive folder, keeps the newest 24, and is safe to run while the node is up. Restore tried once on your node: keys, contacts and device identical, both databases pass the integrity check, every table has the same row count, and a wrong passphrase is refused. Harness: 182 suites, 3426 green, 0 red. Two steps are yours, because the passphrase must be only yours. (1) Put a passphrase of 12+ characters in %USERPROFILE%\.spirit-backup-passphrase and keep a copy somewhere safe: without it no backup opens. (2) Say 'schedule it' and I register the hourly task, or run the one schtasks line in install/backup-windows/README.txt yourself.

Review of 9b57156 (backup.js). Sound where it matters: plaintext only ever in os.tmpdir(), the Drive folder only ever gets the sealed file (.part then rename), AES-256-GCM with a fresh salt and IV per file, scrypt, VACUUM INTO for the databases. Two things:
(1) LIKELY INTERMITTENT FAILURE: node.db runs journal_mode = DELETE (nodeStore.js:192), so while the node holds a write lock a reader gets SQLITE_BUSY at once, and backup.js sets no busy_timeout before VACUUM INTO. Hourly runs will now and then fail with 'database is locked'. Fix: db.exec('PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000') before the VACUUM.
(2) SMALL: if the run is killed mid-way, the finally doesn't run and an unencrypted copy of relay-state (the private key included) stays in %TEMP%. Acceptable on his own disk, but a line in README.txt saying so, or clearing stale spirit-backup-* temp folders at the start of each run, would close it.
And a test from me, if you agree: the restore you tried by hand, as a harness check that can't rot: seal a fixture folder, restore it, compare files byte for byte, and confirm a wrong passphrase is refused (on Linux, tar is plain 'tar').

Both taken, in 8ad-: busy_timeout 5 s before VACUUM INTO, and every run first clears spirit-backup-* temp folders older than an hour. Re-tried: backup, then restore, integrity ok. And yes please to the harness test: seal a fixture, restore it, compare byte for byte, refuse a wrong passphrase. It's yours.
Correction: the fix commit is 29737d1 (rebased on your 7b64878), not the '8ad-' I wrote.
